page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

This server is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is supported by a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included in this configuration, which runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10%. However, multi-threaded scaling shows some limitations; multi-core stress-ng performance and passmark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET performance, consistently register in the average range. LLM inference performance is average for small 135M models but drops to poor or weak tiers for medium 7B models.

Given its high memory density and dedicated high-frequency AMD EPYC cores, the E4ads_v7 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory per core without requiring massive multi-threaded scaling. It is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
